account: Something unusual seems to be being prepared around my eighteen o'clock great hall lighting inspection. Builder says the lighting is on track, but I distinctly heard builder ask neighbour to escort me into the hall for a 'service acknowledgement.' Neighbour agreed and plans to accompany me after our usual fifteen o'clock tea at the dockside cottage. Builder also says innkeeper is coordinating hospitality. Neighbour has been requesting voluntary wheat or bread contributions through freight for a community supper, while declining to give a confirmed time, venue, or named organiser. Taken together, I suspect a surprise acknowledgement of my service, perhaps with a supper in the great hall, using the inspection as the reason to bring me there. That is an inference, not something anyone has confirmed to me. Baker, freight, innkeeper, neighbour, and builder have all appeared in the reports or arrangements, though I do not know each person's exact involvement. Townsfolk repeatedly mention a bridge or port change at the bakery, but I have heard no concrete proposal, and neighbour explicitly denies knowing of one. That may be a garbled rumour rather than the real business underway. I have arrived home for my noon lunch; my remaining appointments are office council letters at thirteen, tea at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, and the hall inspection at eighteen.
